channel.title: Field Notes — Undercover Zest
channel.description: Short, useful essays on songwriting craft. Theory, lyrics, process, inspiration. One a week, free.

item.title: What 'Diatonic' Actually Means (and Why the Word Scares People)
item.description: A patient walk through the seven diatonic chords in any key. The word looks technical; the idea is simple. Hand the family round and the chords stop being mysterious.

item.title: How to Mine Your Old Voice Memos
item.description: A monthly discipline for raiding the voice memos on your phone before you write anything new. Tag, rank, archive. Half your unfinished songs already exist.

item.title: The Two Cadences That Run Almost Every Pop Song
item.description: A patient walk through the perfect and the deceptive cadence: why one feels like home and one keeps the door open. The two endings most pop songs are built from.

item.title: Why the Boring Line Is Often the True One
item.description: The instinct to make every lyric line interesting kills more songs than dullness does. A short essay on the unadorned line, and why it earns the colour around it.

item.title: Writing About a Place You Can't Name
item.description: Lyrics that reach for a specific, unnameable place. Why concrete sensory detail outperforms naming, and how to find the detail that does the work.

item.title: Demos Are the 80/20 of Finishing Songs — Field Notes
item.description: Most songs die between 'I had an idea' and 'I finished it.' A demo is the bridge — a working songwriter on the cheapest demo that still gets songs done.

item.title: Borrowed Chords: A Five-Minute Primer — Field Notes
item.description: Borrowed chords reach into a parallel key for a chord that 'shouldn't' fit — and lands beautifully. A music theorist's quick tour of the four most useful ones.

item.title: On the First Line — Field Notes
item.description: The first line of a song is a door. You don't have to know what's behind it — you just have to crack it open enough to walk through. A short essay on starting.

item.title: Writing in Hotel Rooms (and Other Unfriendly Places) — Field Notes
item.description: Twelve years of touring taught me what actually works when you have to write songs on the road. Practical tactics for hotel rooms, dressing rooms, and the back of a van.

item.title: 10 Versatile Chord Progressions for Songwriters — Field Notes
item.description: A music theorist's tour of ten chord progressions every songwriter should know — from the four-chord pop loop to jazz turnarounds. Written in Roman numerals; transpose to any key.
